questions.question:
Which two numbers, from amongst the given options, should be interchanged to make the given equation correct?

15 - 4 + (8 × 6) ÷ 16 + 9 × 3 - 7 = 31
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is 

By using BODMAS Rule (Brackets of division, multiplication, addition, subtraction) and going with the

options,

Option 1) 6 and 16

 Given equation:15 - 4 + (8 × 6) ÷ 16 + 9 × 3 - 7 = 31

 By interchanging 6 and 16 in the given equation.

 Interchanged equation is : 15 - 4 +(8 × 16) ÷ 6 + 9 × 3 - 7 = 31

 = 15 - 4 + **128 ÷ 6** + 27 - 7 =31

 = **15** - 4 **+ 21.333 + 20** = 31

= 56.33 - 4 = 31

= 52.333 ≠ 31 

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 2) 4 and 6

 Given equation:15 - 4 + (8 × 6) ÷ 16 + 9 × 3 - 7 = 31

 By interchanging 4 and 6 in given equation.

Interchanged equation is:15 - 6 + (8 × 4) ÷ 16 + 9 × 3 - 7 = 31

= 15 - 6 + **32 ÷ 16** + 27 - 7 = 31

= **15** - 6 **+ 2 + 20** = 31

= **37 - 6** = 31

= 31 = 31

⇒ LHS = RHS

Option 3): 8 and 16

Given equation:15 - 4 + (8 × 6) ÷ 16 + 9 × 3 - 7 = 31

By interchanging 8 and 16 in given equation.

Interchanged equation is: 15 - 4 + **(16 × 6)** ÷ 8 + 9 × 3 - 7 = 31

= 15 - 4 + **96 ÷ 8** + 27 - 7 =31

= **15** - 4 **+ 12 + 7** = 31

= 15 - 4 + 12 + 7 = 31

= **34 - 4** = 31

=30 ≠ 31

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 4): 4 and 3

Given equation: 15 - 4 + (8 × 6) ÷ 16 + 9 × 3 - 7 = 31

By interchanging 4 and 3 in given equation.

Interchanged equation is: 15 - 3 + **(8 × 6)** ÷ 16 + 9 × 4 - 7 = 31

= 15 - 3 + **48 ****÷ 16** + 9 × 4 - 7 = 31

= 15 - 3 + 3 + **9 × 4** - 7 = 3

= **15 **- 3 **+ 3 + 36 **- 7 = 31

= **54 - 3 - 7 **= 31

= 44 ≠ 31

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Thus, the correct answer is** 4 and 6.**

questions.question: If 2ⁿd Oct 2003 is Thursday, then what will be the day of the week on 15th July 2010?
questions.solution:
Given: **2nd October 2003** was Thursday.

Now,

2003 to 2010 = 7 Years (5 Ordinary Year and 2 Leap Year).

So, 2 Leap Year has 4 odd days,

And, 5 Ordinary Year has 5 odd days.

Total odd days = 4 + 5 = 9.

9 odd days → 9/7 = 1 week and 2 odd days.

questions.question:
Read the following information carefully and answer the question given below:

'P & Q' means 'P is the son of Q'.

'P @ Q' means 'P is the brother of Q'.

'P % Q' means 'P is the sister of Q'.

'P $ Q' means 'P is the daughter of Q'.

'P # Q' means 'P is the father of Q'.

How is W related to Z, in the expression 'V & W # T @ X % Y $ Z' ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fb0803aeca2b730c642d4ccdfaaa344c817c9d7877eb63c5486d15a149fd3a5f.png] 

Given:

 
 

 P is
 
 

 Symbol
 &
 @
 %
 $
 #
 
 

 Meaning
 Son
 Brother
 Sister
 Daughter
 Father
 
 

 of Q
 
 

 

Expression:- V & W # T @ X % Y $ Z

Here,

V & W means V is the son of W.

W # T means W is the father of T.

T @ X means T is the brother of X.

X % Y means X is the sister of Y.

Y $ Z means Y is the daughter of Z

Thus, the following family tree can be drawn:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5ec68a4d9589581a51888805a01ca610389c35a9c3ac8ed554516bb6bae17493.png] 

W is the husband of Z.

Hence, the correct answer is __Husband__.

If 'A' stands for '÷', 'B' stands for '×', 'C' stands for '+' and 'D' stands for, '-' what will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation?

83 C 7 B 539 A 49 D 29 = ?

Three Statements are given followed by four conclusions numbered 1, 2, 3,and 4. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically does NOT follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All P are G.

Some G are B.

All B are C.

**Conclusions:**

1) All P being C is a possibility.

2) Some P are B.

3) Some C are G.

4) Some G are P
questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d8569b2085fc31f58f8dde7c4edcd65a00520878fe4597d065c882d470eac688.png] 

Conclusions:

1) All P being C is a possibility → Follow (As all P are G, some G are B and all B are C. So, as no negative or cross relation between P and C is given, therefore it is definitely true)

2) Some P are B → Does not follow (As all P are G and some G are B. So, it is possible but not definitely true)

3) Some C are G → Follow (As some G are B and all B are C. So, as Some part of G are B which whole comes in C, therefore it is definitely true)

4) Some G are P → Follow (As all P are G. So, Some G are P is definitely true)

∴ Here, All conclusions follows, except conclusion - (2).​

Hence, the correct answer is **"Only 2nd does not follow**"

questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number.

17 : 78 : : 15 : 68 : : 28 : ?
questions.solution:
The logic here is:

**Logic: first number × 4 + (first number - 7) = Second number**

17 : 78 Rightarrow 17 × 4 + (17 - 7) = 68 + 10 = 78

15 : 68 Rightarrow 15 × 4 + (15 - 7) = 60 + 8 = 68

Thus, we will have for

28: ? Rightarrow 28 × 4 + (28 - 7) = 112 + 21 = 133

Hence, the missing number is __**133**__.

questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set.

(50, 10, 15)

(60, 10, 16)

(NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: **(3rd number - 2nd number) × 2nd number = 1st number**.

Now,

For, (50, 10, 15)

→ (15 - 10) × 10

→ 5 × 10 = 50.

For, (60, 10, 16)

→ (16 - 10) × 10

→ 6 × 10 = 60.

Similarly, for **(60, 15, 19)**

**→ (19 - 15) × 15**

**→ 4 × 15 = 60.**

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 1"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

The pattern followed here is: 

**Logic: **In each pair the 1st number is divided by the 2nd number and the answer is added to the 2nd number to get the 3rd number.

1) (50, 10, 15 ): 50 ÷ 10 = 5, 10 + 5 = 15

2) (60, 10, 16): 60 ÷ 10 = 6, 10 + 6 = 16

Next, we will check all the options one by one:

1) **(60, 15, 19): 60 ÷ 15 = 4, 15 + 4 = 19**

2) (60, 10, 6): 60 ÷ 10 = 6, 10 + 6 = 16 ≠ 6. This is not true. 

3) (80, 20, 16): 80 ÷ 20 = 4, 20 + 4 = 24 ≠16. This is not true. 

4) (80, 6, 15): 80 ÷ 6 = 13.33, 6 + 13.33 = 19.333 ≠ 15. This is not true.

Hence, the correct answer is **"(60, 15, 19)".**
